text:
marta: quick heads-up from today's usability lab: SLO threshold input had an affordance problem. users couldn't tell if they were entering % or absolute counts while typing.

jess: saw that too. one tester typed `80` then switched metric and the preview flipped to counts without warning. they assumed their change didn't save.

rohith: can you share steps to reproduce? want to confirm frontend state sync issue.

marta: repro: SLOs -> edit -> click threshold field -> type `80` -> rapidly toggle metric selector -> unit label blinks out, preview sometimes shows route default metric instead of the SLO override. chrome + firefox.

sam: probable race between controlled input state and the metric selector prop. front-end only renders unit on blur. easy fix: surface a persistent inline unit chip while focus is inside the field.

jess: design note: prefer a subtle trailing unit chip inside the input rather than appending `%` in the value. keeps keyboard behavior predictable.

rohith: agree. accessibility note: if unit is purely decorative we still need it in the accessible name. add `aria-describedby` pointing to visually-hidden unit text.

a11y-bot: Recommendation: include unit in `aria-label` or add `aria-describedby` reference. For inline validation, use `role=\"status\"` on the error node so screen readers announce messages immediately. Also check color contrast for helper text (need >= 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large).

marta: for helper copy, two quick options: (A) "Enter a threshold, e.g., 95% or 1000 requests." (B) "Specify a percent (e.g., 95%) or count (e.g., 1000)." which is cleaner?

jess: A wins in tests — concrete examples reduce ambiguity.

sam: implementation item: parse input tolerantly. allow `95`, `95%`, `0.95` and normalize to backend canonical (fraction). I'll add a small parser. Example we can use:```js
function parseThreshold(input, metricType){
  // returns fraction for pct, integer for count
  if(metricType === 'pct'){
    const n = Number(input.toString().replace(/%/g, ''));
    return isNaN(n) ? null : n > 1 ? n/100 : n;
  }
  return Number(input);
}
```

rohith: nice. add unit tests for `95`, `95%`, `0.95`. also add client-side validation error: "Percentages should be between 0 and 100".

a11y-bot: Also ensure error text meets contrast and is reachable by keyboard focus. Error container should be announced and focusable if it's critical.

marta: UI changes to spec: 1) inline trailing unit chip visible while input focused; 2) helper text beneath the field with example copy (use option A); 3) parser + normalization in client; 4) preview widget should respect explicit SLO unit (prefer override over route default); 5) a11y notes: aria-describedby + role=status + contrast >= 4.5 for helper/error if small text.

jess: small UX detail: when users increment with arrow keys, keep the caret behavior consistent. don't put the chip inside the caret flow. prefer absolute-positioned chip inside input container.

sam: got it. i'll implement chip as a pseudo-element and strip `%` before editing. will open PR and tag y'all.

rohith: telemetry: log `slo_threshold_input_normalized` and `slo_preview_metric_mismatch` with attributes so we can detect regressions.

marta: i'll update Figma with two states (focused with chip + populated with unit outside value) and post link here. also will add copy and a11y checklist.

jess: thanks — once Figma link is up i'll pick final copy and review contrast values.

a11y-bot: Final reminder: test with VoiceOver/NVDA and keyboard-only nav. Use `aria-hidden=true` for visual-only elements and ensure accessible text is available elsewhere.

sam: thanks team. assigning to sprint after PR review.

marta: end thread. will post Figma + PR link when ready :rocket:
